 Bag it, don’t blow it!
 Rake leaves and yard debris and bundle or place in a trash bag for collection. Leaves and grass clippings left on driveways, sidewalks, and roads wash away into our local lakes and degrade water quality.
 Blowing yard waste down the storm drain is a violation of City Code. Make sure your hired lawn care professionals aren’t improperly disposing of your yard waste. Ultimately, you can be fined for their actions on your property. Learn more here .

Drop-off - Household Hazardous Waste
Drop off this item for safe disposal.
 Hazardous waste is anything labeled with the words flammable, poison, warning, corrosive, explosive, danger, pesticide, caustic, or acid. Also, look on the label for symbols designating these properties. Latex or oil-based paint and items containing mercury, such as fluorescent lights and thermostats are also considered hazardous waste.
 Improper disposal of these waste materials can pollute the environment and pose a threat to human health. Household hazardous waste can cause physical injury to sanitation workers, contaminate septic tanks or wastewater treatment systems if poured down drains or toilets. They can also present hazards to children and pets if left around the house. Never allow hazardous waste to enter into a storm drain.
 Find safer options that may replace your household hazardous waste items. Learn more about household hazardous waste .
